title: I one-shotted a Steam game with Claude and ChatGPT. It only took 1,574 prompts and 15 months.
author: Pix4Geeks
selftext:
After a year and a half working on Kyūten, its Steam page is finally live :) I wish I did it sooner though...

And yes, the title is a joke. I can see one prompt producing a super basic gameplay prototype. Getting from that to a game I’d actually want people to play took quite a bit more work \^\^

I've played a lot to Final fantasy, and especially the VIII and its card game Triple Triad. Kyūten's rules are based on it.

You place cards on a board and flip your opponent’s cards by beating the values on their sides. 

The board grows as you climb the Nine Heavens, and you can borrow powers from guardians inspired by Japanese mythology. When a run ends, you keep the cards you collected for the next attempt.

Claude and ChatGPT helped me along the way. There was also a lot of testing, changing my mind, breaking things, and trying again. As a business analyst in real life, I'm used to 😁

I’ve used AI tools for some visuals, music, and translation help too; nothing is generated during gameplay.

The game is planned for later this year. If you have a look at the page, I’d be curious to hear what you think of the card battles, especially if you played way too much Triple Triad too :)

https://store.steampowered.com/app/5333100/Kyuten

Pix'

replies.author: Pix4Geeks
replies.body:
To be fair, it's not 15 full months. But here's a summary :   
\- started with chatGPT chat to create the prototype : a simple copy of triple triad (no power, no roguelite, just the 3x3 board with cards). It was kind of a hassle to keep things working because I copied/pasted in godot and chatGPT

\- that's when I made a break because I didn't imagine being able to deliver a full game with this process

\- then I discovered Claude Code. Before starting, I wrote a complete GDD (around 1400 .md rows) with the help of Claude to define the scope of the project. This only took quite some times.

\- and finally I went back and forth between Claude code and Codex depending on the model-to-follow moment.

Art has been done with Nano banana at first, but have been reworked by GPT Images 2.5

Music is made by Suno

SFX are open source ones.



If I had to start now, I'll keep the GDD part, for sure. Even if it has changed a bit over time, the base of the game is defined here. The rules, the lore, the limits of the project (to avoid ideas like, ok the game works, let's make it multiplayer live-service game, with real money boosters., etc.. \^\^)  
And one thing I will change for future projects : create the Steam page earlier. Now, my game is ready. But I need to take time to do some marketing... If the page was ready before, I could have already done that. 

About changes, I now also use a lot more the agents features. Like I have one agent who orchestrates different sub-agents (coder, reviewer) instead of creating one agent per development phase.

comments.body: as a new AI-empowered game dev, how hard is it to push an AI game through Steam? how long does it take? My game will be ready for release in about a month but i've never published anything yet...

replies.author: Pix4Geeks
replies.body:
It takes few weeks for the 1st one.   
1. they need to confirm your id, this takes around 10 working days  
2. they need to control the store page : 5-7 wd  
3. they need to control the package : 5-7 wd
